info.name: paccradle API: exports (2026-10-30)
info.description:
Change: M1-D7, exports endpoints (2026-10-30). The client contract moves to **1.0.0-beta.6** (`api-version`); the admin contract stays at 1.0.0-beta.2. Merge into the main contract.

**New:** `POST` and `GET /api/client/v1/designs/{design_id}/exports`, `GET /api/client/v1/exports/{export_id}`. **New codes:** `DESIGN_NOT_BUILDABLE` (422, `meta.detail` in English), `EXPORT_PAYMENT_REQUIRED` (402, `meta.checkout` and `meta.offers` for Paddle.js), `EXPORT_NOT_FOUND` (404), `EXPORT_FAILED` (an export's stored error). `AUTH_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` (403) now also answers a guest's export.

**Checkout:** `Paddle.Checkout.open({ items: [{ priceId: meta.checkout.price_id, quantity: 1 }], customer: { email: meta.checkout.customer_email }, customData: meta.checkout.custom_data })`. The purchase unlocks the design when Paddle's webhook lands (M1-F4); until then the 402 stays.

request.description:
Asks for files from the design's current version. **Needs an account**: a guest gets `AUTH_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` (403) and the web app opens sign-up (DEC-14).

- `formats`: any of `svg`, `pdf`, `dxf` (production files, **paid**) and `png` (watermarked preview), `test_print` (watermarked print-at-home PDF; needs `paper`), which are **free**. Repeats are ignored.
- `paper`: `a4` or `letter`, for the test print.
- `version`: the version the user is looking at; another one is `DESIGN_VERSION_CONFLICT` (409).

The design is generated first: one that can't be made yet is `DESIGN_NOT_BUILDABLE` (422) and costs nothing. Production files are covered, in this order, by: the design's unlock if this version was saved within its 30-day edit window (`paid_with: unlocked`); Pro (`pro`, unlocks the design for 30 days); one export credit (`credit`, spent now, unlocks for 30 days). Otherwise **402 `EXPORT_PAYMENT_REQUIRED`**: open Paddle.js with `meta.checkout` (`price_id`, `custom_data`, `customer_email`); `meta.offers` has the pack and Pro prices. After paying, ask again.

**202** with the pending export: poll `GET /exports/{export_id}`. At most 60 exports an hour per user.

request.description: The caller's export. Once `done`, each file has a link that works for 5 minutes and downloads under `file_name`; fetch the export again for new links (files are kept: re-downloading never expires). `failed` carries `error` (`EXPORT_FAILED`): ask again, at no cost. Someone else's export is `EXPORT_NOT_FOUND`.
